stack.frontend: HTMX 2.0.4 + Tailwind v4 (committed app.css artifact) + vanilla-JS widgets
stack.deployment: native binaries + systemd on Raspberry Pi (ultron-ap unprivileged + ultron-helper root over a Unix socket)

implementation_notes: FR-079 — the mute filter sits in Dispatcher.send(), which drops the telegram notifier from THIS event's fan-out (withoutChannel copies the slice; mutating the cached notifier list would turn a 4h mute into a permanent one). The notifier stays a dumb transport and the FR-024 storm cache is never touched for a muted event. NotificationMuteUntil fails OPEN — any error, a missing row or an unparseable expiry means muted=false, because silently swallowing a critical alert is the one outcome worse than an unwanted notification.

FR-080 — DigestScheduler.Tick(now) takes the clock as a parameter, so every AC ('given this stored state at this instant, does exactly one email go out?') is asserted exactly, with no sleeps and no wall-clock races. MarkDigestSent is written on COMPLETION, success or failure: marking only on success would retry a dead SMTP relay every tick for the rest of the hour (~60 sends).

FR-081 — the drawer reuses the existing allow-listed 'logs' helper action over the same Unix socket; no new privileged verb, no new capability. The unit name is validated against systemd.IsValidServiceName — the SAME authority start/stop/restart uses (exported for this purpose so a second, divergent regex could not drift) — and the root helper re-validates independently.

FR-082/FR-083 — one SQLite read on settings render, one write on save. No goroutine, no GPIO/I2C, no daemon connection: the owner required this stay lightweight after a previous hardware-control attempt cost the Pi significant CPU and memory. The section carries a visible note so the admin is never misled into thinking the fan is being driven.

The hardware section and the mute row reuse the existing widget vocabulary (segmented / toggle / chip-preset / stepper) and bind through settings.js — no page-level inline <script> returns to any template (CSS7 / NFR-087). The drawer's open/close lives in a new widget (web/static/js/widgets/service-logs.js) following the same BG-038 lifecycle: head-loaded, idempotent guards, re-init on htmx:afterSwap and htmx:historyRestore.
security_notes: A real defect was found and fixed while building AC-081-003: internal/logfilter's secret-key pattern used \b(token|secret|password|…), and \b never matches between '_' and 'token' — so bot_token=…, api_token=… and ULTRON_SECRET_KEY: … sailed through the journal filter unredacted. The pattern now consumes surrounding word runs ([\w.\-]* on both sides). This hardens the /logs page and the root helper too, not just the new drawer. Regression test: TestFilter_RedactsPrefixedSecretKeys.

The drawer re-applies logfilter in the panel even though the helper already redacts before the bytes cross the socket — defence in depth, so a future caller reaching the drawer by another path (or an older helper build) still cannot render a leaked token into the browser.
Journal content is attacker-influenceable (any process can write to the journal). It is rendered through html/template into a <pre> — escaped, never innerHTML.
All three new/extended POST routes go through the existing CSRF middleware; the drawer is a GET behind requireAuth.

deviations.spec: an unauthenticated drawer request 'is redirected to /login'
deviations.built: the panel answers /api/* with 401 Unauthorized (existing middleware contract — htmx turns it into a login redirect client-side). Substance of the AC holds: no journal output is returned and the helper is never called. The drawer inherits the existing auth posture rather than growing a second one; changing the middleware would alter every other /api route.
deviations.test: TC-ACG-081Ef asserts 401 + no journal content + zero helper calls.

deviations.spec: an injection-shaped unit name is rejected with 400
deviations.built: true for --version, foo;rm, -Mroot and 'foo bar'. A literal '..' never reaches the handler at all: net/http's mux normalises the path and 301s first. Either way no journalctl runs.
deviations.test: TC-ACG-081Bf asserts 400 for the injection shapes, non-200 for '..', and zero helper calls in all cases.

technical_debt.substitution: The fan-mode selector persists its value; nothing actuates the Pironman fan (no PWM/GPIO write, no daemon connection). Declared in the feature's no_go_zone and confirmed by the owner on 2026-07-13: a previous hardware-control attempt cost the Pi significant CPU and memory, and hardware actuation cannot be verified in CI. The persisted schema is exactly what a future actuator would read, so no rework is created.
technical_debt.reason: Owner constraint (Pi resource cost) + not verifiable without the physical Pironman board.
technical_debt.remediation: A follow-up feature would add a small actuator that reads HardwareConfig.fan_mode and drives the Pironman daemon, with a measured CPU/memory budget.

technical_debt.substitution: The OLED configuration persists (enabled + metric); nothing writes to the OLED panel. Same rationale and same no_go_zone entry as FR-082.
technical_debt.reason: Owner constraint (Pi resource cost) + not verifiable without the physical panel.
technical_debt.remediation: Same follow-up actuator would read HardwareConfig.oled_enabled / oled_metric.

technical_debt.substitution: The log drawer's browser behaviour (open → fetch → collapse) is verified by the Go tests through the real Unix socket against a fake helper, plus a Chrome pass over the rest of the feature UI. The drawer itself could NOT be exercised in the browser here: the dev host is macOS and has no systemd, so /services renders its unavailable state and has no rows. The project has no headless-browser stack in CI (same precedent as settings-revamp FR-063 and help-page FR-050/051/053).
technical_debt.reason: No systemd on the dev host; no browser CI infrastructure in the project.
technical_debt.remediation: Exercise the drawer once on the Pi itself (192.168.1.29) after deploy — open a failing unit's drawer and confirm the tail renders, then collapse it.

verification.feature_tests: 36 test cases, all passing (go test ./... -run TestTC_ACG)
verification.browser: 14/14 checks in Chrome against the running app: hardware section (accordion, anchor chip, fan segmented, OLED toggle + metric, save → applied pill → persists across reload), Telegram mute (chip row → 4h → muted state with countdown → cancel restores the chip row), daily digest (toggle, hour stepper bounded 0–23, save persists). Two markup defects were found and fixed by this pass: the OLED toggle did not follow toggle.js's data-toggle-input contract, and the mute chip-preset wrote to a hidden input that chip-preset.js does not drive.
